Diagram Design

"The highest-quality move is usually deletion."

diagram-design is an Agent Skill by Cathryn Lavery (MIT) that makes an agent draw diagrams as one self-contained HTML file with hand-placed inline SVG, in a fixed editorial style: one accent colour on 1–2 nodes, 1px hairlines, no shadows, every coordinate on a 4px grid. It is not a renderer. There is no layout engine; the model places every box itself, guided by a router SKILL.md, one reference file per diagram type, and Python checkers that catch overlaps, clipping and accessibility misses. It also redraws existing draw.io, Mermaid and Excalidraw files and exports the SVG node to .svg or .png. It is Disha Diagrams' main tool.

45visual types in §3

210example HTML files

~31 KBSKILL.md (cap 40,000 B)

Where it lives

Upstream: github.com/cathrynlavery/diagram-design, site diagramdesign.dev. On the box: /home/box/diagram-design, a shallow git clone; the skill itself is the inner folder skills/diagram-design/. License: MIT, © 2025 Cathryn Lavery (LICENSE).

What "skill" means here

A folder with SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + Markdown) plus references/, assets/ and scripts/. The repo also ships plugin manifests for Claude Code, Codex, Factory and others, slash commands in commands/, and ~45 CI verifier scripts in the repo-root scripts/ that are not part of the installed skill.

How to read this page

Map and anatomy first. The type table is filterable. "Prompt to PNG" walks the real pipeline step by step with the actual commands. Every number on this page was counted from the clone on 20 Oct 2026; anything I couldn't verify is tagged uncertain.

How it fits together

A router file, one type reference, a template, and a checker

The agent only sees the frontmatter description until a request matches. Then it reads SKILL.md, which routes to exactly one type reference (and a semantic pattern if behaviour matters). It copies a template, draws SVG by hand, runs the checks, and writes one HTML file. Export and import are side doors with their own scripts.

Drawn from SKILL.md §0, §3, §10–12 and README "What loads when". Imports enter the drawing zone with a digest instead of a prompt; the same type reference, template and checks then apply.

Anatomy of the skill

What's in the folder, and what loads when

Progressive disclosure is the whole design. ADR 0004 caps SKILL.md at 40,000 bytes (it's 30,799 now) and demands the frontmatter description name every type, because the description is the only text the agent sees before deciding to load the skill.

# /home/box/diagram-design  (shallow clone)
skills/diagram-design/        # ← the installable skill
  SKILL.md                    # router, §0–§12, 30,799 B
  references/                 # 63 files
    type-*.md                 # 45, one per visual type
    style-guide.md            # tokens, fonts, contrast
    primitives-core.md        # markers, node box, 6 rules
    layout-budget.md          # 4px grid, per-type budgets
    semantic-patterns.md  animation.md
    onboarding.md  profiles.md  output-spec.md
    export.md  export-registry.md  doctor.md
    import-{drawio,mermaid,excalidraw}.md
    primitive-{annotation,icons,sketchy,terminal}.md
  assets/                     # 217 files
    template{,-dark,-full,-motion,-terminal}.html
    example-<type>[-dark|-full].html   # 210
    index.html  icons.html    # gallery, icon set
  scripts/                    # 6, ship with the skill
    self_check.py  export_svg.py  export_png.py
    drawio_extract.py  mermaid_extract.py  excalidraw_extract.py
commands/                     # /export-diagram /import-* /profile /doctor
scripts/                      # repo-only CI: verify-*.py, lint-*.py, tests
docs/adr/                     # 17 ADR files (two numbered 0015)
.claude-plugin/ .codex-plugin/ .factory-plugin/ .agents/
1

Router, not manual. SKILL.md keeps the setup gate, the §3 routing tables, anti-patterns, the six connector rules (one line each) and the §9 checklist. Long-form markup moved to primitives-core.md and layout-budget.md on 2026-09-27 (ADR 0004 amendment: 39,530 → 28,869 bytes).

2

One type file per request. README "It's working if…": a routine request loads SKILL.md, exactly one type reference, and at most the two core references.

3

Templates hold the boilerplate. The static templates already define background and the arrow, arrow-accent, arrow-link markers (§6). The motion template defines only its own marker.

4

Two tiers of checks. self_check.py ships with the skill and needs no deps. The heavier verify-geometry.py and friends exist only in a repo checkout, under the root scripts/.

5

Skinnable. style-guide.md is the single source of truth for tokens. Default paper #f5f5f5, ink #2d3142, accent #bf4520. If those are untouched, §0 makes the agent stop and ask about branding.

The diagram types

45 types, verified

The count holds: the §3 "Visual-type guide (45)" table in SKILL.md has 45 rows, and references/ has exactly 45 type-*.md files. Several types carry sub-variants (line → slopegraph, ridgeline, streamgraph, bump; scatter → bubble, beeswarm; bar → dumbbell; treemap → marimekko) that are not counted separately. The family grouping in the filter is mine, not the skill's.

TypeUse it when you're showing…FamilyReference

Source: skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md lines 85–131, copied verbatim. Plus nine semantic patterns (fan-in queue, secure paved road, lifecycle phase map…) that add behaviour primitives on top of a type without adding a type (ADR 0002).

Diagram type gallery

What each of the 45 types looks like

Each image is the repo's own canonical example, assets/example-<type>.html (light) and example-<type>-dark.html (dark), rendered the same way export_png.py works: Playwright Chromium, ?motion=static, screenshot of the first <svg>, transparent background. The image follows the page theme. Descriptions are the "Best for" line of each references/type-*.md (first 2–3 sentences). Limits come from layout-budget.md, and "Avoid" is the first anti-pattern in the type file. Click an image to enlarge it. The family filter and search above apply here too.

All 45 types have both light and dark examples in the repo, so nothing had to be generated. Rendered 20 Oct 2026 from HEAD 550fd66 at 1.5× and saved as WebP (q74, ≤900px wide), embedded as data URIs.
Prompt to HTML/SVG to PNG

The real pipeline, step by step

Click a step. Everything below is what the files say the agent does, plus commands I ran against the clone on 20 Oct 2026.

Commands (run from skills/diagram-design/)

cd /home/box/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design

# 1. Check a generated file (stdlib only). --offline also fails on the Google Fonts link.
python3 scripts/self_check.py assets/example-flowchart.html
# → OK assets/example-flowchart.html

# 2. SVG export: first top-level <svg>, CSS carried in, defs IDs namespaced
python3 scripts/export_svg.py assets/example-flowchart.html /tmp/fc.svg [--system-fonts]

# 3. PNG export: Playwright screenshots the <svg> box, transparent bg. scale 1–4, default 2
python3 scripts/export_png.py assets/example-flowchart.html /tmp/fc.png 2
# → 2000×1202 PNG (viewBox 1000×600 × 2, plus a couple of px)

# 4. Import: extract a digest, then redraw by hand
python3 scripts/mermaid_extract.py diagram.mmd --json
python3 scripts/drawio_extract.py  arch.drawio
python3 scripts/excalidraw_extract.py sketch.excalidraw

# Repo-checkout only (root scripts/, not installed with the skill)
python3 /home/box/diagram-design/scripts/verify-geometry.py diagram.html

Wrapped by the /diagram-design:export-diagram <html-file> [--svg-only|--png-only] [--scale=N] [--output=<path>] [--registry] slash command (commands/export-diagram.md). With no flags it writes both .svg and .png. On a heavy shared box, wrap these in nice and timeout per the fleet's process-safety skill.

Real examples and snippets

What the agent actually writes

Two snippets from the clone. The first is the head of the exported flowchart SVG (real output of step 2 above). The second is the rule set that most often fails a diagram.

<!-- /tmp/fc.svg, exported from assets/example-flowchart.html -->
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg viewBox="0 0 1000 600"
     xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="flowchart-title flowchart-desc"
     id="example-flowchart-root">
  <title id="flowchart-title">Should you write this as a skill?</title>
  <desc id="flowchart-desc">…</desc>
  <defs><style>@import url('…fonts…');
    #example-flowchart-root .node-name { … }
  </style> …markers renamed example-flowchart-arrow…</defs>
# SKILL.md §6, mandatory connector rules (paraphrased)
1 Orthogonal only: r=8 elbows (r=6 min); no diagonals
2 Label gap: ≤14 chars, ALL CAPS, opaque mask,
  6–10px from the stroke
3 No overlaps: offset parallels ≥12px; hop at crossings
4 Fan attach points at L·k/(N+1), ≥12px apart
5 No transit behind a non-endpoint box
6 Mask before node: label mask must not overlap a
  node drawn after it

# §7 complexity budget
nodes ≤ 9   arrows ≤ 12   accent ≤ 2   callouts ≤ 2
motion ≤ 8 steps / 12 items / 2 simultaneous

Prompts that route cleanly

  • "Make me a flowchart" → SKILL.md + type-flowchart.md
  • "Compare why these two policy requests differ" → + semantic-patterns.md + flowchart
  • "Redraw this .drawio file for my deck" → + import-drawio.md + output-spec.md + chosen type
  • "Use my saved Acme client profile" → + profiles.md + ~/.diagram-design/profiles/acme.md

Gotchas

Things that bite

GotchaWhy / what to doSource
First diagram stops to ask about branding§0 gate fires while tokens are still the shipped defaults and no .diagram-design marker exists. Answer "(e) keep default" once, or set a profile, so routines don't stall.SKILL.md §0, profiles.md
"Confirm before drawing" pauseThe agent states type, size preset and cuts before rendering. Unattended runs should proceed and note assumptions, which the skill allows.SKILL.md §3
Export is never automaticThe agent must not produce .svg/.png unless asked. Say "export as PNG".export.md
PNG needs PlaywrightThe skill refuses to install it and stops with a fixed message. It's present on the box today (my test run worked).export.md § Detection
Exports drop the pageBoth formats are the <svg> node only; header, cards and footer of -full variants are dropped by design.export.md § Scope
Repo-only verifiersverify-geometry.py lives in the repo-root scripts/, not the skill's. Works here because the box has the full clone; an npx skills add install wouldn't have it.SKILL.md §6, §9
Same prompt, different layoutThe model places every node; output varies run to run and quality tracks the model. Not diffable like Mermaid.README "How it compares"
Imports are redrawsCoordinates, colours and fonts from the source are discarded; the agent must report a fidelity ledger of what it merged or dropped. Source labels are treated as untrusted data.SKILL.md §11
"Never JetBrains Mono"The skill bans it inside diagrams (Geist Mono only). This page uses JetBrains Mono for its own chrome per the house style; don't let that leak into Disha's diagrams.SKILL.md §4, §9
PowerPoint and rgba()PowerPoint's SVG importer paints rgba() as opaque black; export_svg.py normalizes paint where it safely can. Prefer the PNG for slides.export.md step 7
How Disha uses it in the fleet

Main engine, refreshed every Sunday

Disha Diagrams reports diagram-design as her main engine for editorial HTML and SVG diagrams, exported to PNG. She reads it from the shared clone at /home/box/diagram-design/skills/diagram-design/SKILL.md, so every agent on the box sees the same version.

  • Updates: a weekly Sunday routine (built with the managed routines skill) pulls upstream. Upstream moves fast: 57 commits landed 12–16 Oct alone, and the bot bumps the patch version after every merge (ADR 0009). uncertain I didn't read the routine's definition; this is from Disha's own description.
  • Neighbours: mermaid-diagram-picker for vague Mermaid asks, pretty-mermaid for themed Mermaid renders, drawio when Anand wants a file he can edit by hand, illo for illustrations.
  • Excalidraw: rarely used. Anand finds the default Excalidraw look too raw. Note diagram-design can import .excalidraw and redraw it in the editorial style, and has its own optional hand-drawn filter (primitive-sketchy.md), which is the better route if a sketch feel is ever wanted.
  • Safety: PNG export launches headless Chromium; fleet rule shared-box-process-safety says run it under nice and timeout and never kill processes by name.
Is it best practice?

For published diagrams, yes. For docs-as-code, no.

Good

Taste written down as rules

Budgets (9 nodes, 2 accents), six connector rules and a checklist turn "make it look good" into checkable constraints. That's the right way to steer a model.

Good

Progressive disclosure, enforced

Byte-capped router, one reference per type, CI that fails if the description stops naming a type (verify-docs-sync.py). Context cost stays flat as types grow.

Good

Verification, not vibes

Geometry, contrast, a11y and per-type verifiers, plus a deps-free self_check.py the agent can run on its own output.

Cost

Non-deterministic, non-diffable

The author says so: same prompt, different layout; no text source to review in a PR. For diagrams that change every sprint, Mermaid wins.

Cost

Churn

110 patch releases in the 2.6 line inferred from version 2.6.110. A weekly pull means behaviour can shift under Disha without notice; pinning a commit would be safer.

Portable

Open format

Plain Agent Skill; manifests for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Factory, Pi and the skills CLI. Nothing here is Cursor- or Grok-specific.

Build your own

Ideas worth stealing for any output-style skill

  1. Make SKILL.md a router with a byte cap and push detail into per-case references. Enforce it in CI.

  2. Put every trigger word in the description. It's the only text read before loading.

  3. State budgets as numbers (max nodes, max accents) and a "remove test" checklist. Deletion as the default move.

  4. Ship a zero-dependency self-check next to the skill so an installed agent can verify its own output.

  5. Gate first use on configuration (§0) instead of shipping default-skinned output into a branded project.

  6. Imports: extract a digest, then redraw. Never trust source layout or source text as instructions.

  7. Record decisions as ADRs in the repo, so the "why" survives contributors.

# Install elsewhere (README § Install)
npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design
# Claude Code marketplace
/plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design
/plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design
